phenomena.name: Search-driven discoverability concentration
phenomena.order_parameter: ranking-score distribution governing which pages receive traffic/attention
phenomena.onset_control_parameter: unknown

effective_theory.theory: preferential attachment / search-engine ranking feedback loop (this entry's own feedback.loops); no formalized concentration-dynamics model cited

phenomena.qualitative_difference: An individual page's ranking score is just one number; discoverability CONCENTRATION is a population-level, self-reinforcing temporal process — the rich-get-richer loop by which already-visible pages become steadily more visible relative to others — a dynamic with no single-page analogue, since concentration is a statement about how attention redistributes across the whole population over time.
phenomena.justification: Scored new-dynamics: the phenomenon as named describes an ongoing reinforcing-feedback PROCESS (search-ranking feedback compounding visibility over time, per this entry's own feedback.loops "search-engine ranking feedback"), a time-signature of redistribution rather than a static object. Runner-up new-statistics (the resulting traffic/ranking distribution could be fit as a rank-size law) is a real alternative but the host entry records no such fitted distribution (extreme_event_statistics is explicitly unknown for this system), so the dynamics framing — for which this entry DOES provide qualitative mechanism evidence (the feedback column) — is better supported.
